classification.difficultyReason: Extend the supplied partition models by subdividing halves into equal pieces and identifying each piece relative to the whole; completed examples scaffold the method.

content.prompt: Complete the pattern below. These show partition division. “what is the size of each part?”

spec.description: Three equal-width bars: a labelled half, each half subdivided into two, then four cells with the first highlighted and labelled one quarter.
spec.mathematics: Partition one half into two equal parts; each part is one quarter of the whole.
spec.answerVisibility: The completed model and blue equation are permanent source-printed demonstrations.

answer.worked:
The whole contains four equal parts after each half is split into two. One resulting part is $\frac14$ of the whole.
$$\frac12\div2=\frac14$$

spec.description: Half model, subdivision into thirds of each half, and six-cell result with the first cell highlighted and labelled one sixth.
spec.mathematics: One half split into three equal pieces gives one sixth of the whole.
spec.answerVisibility: Preserve the supplied one-sixth diagram label; omit the separate teacher answer from the unsolved equation.

answer.worked:
Split each half into three equal pieces. The whole contains six equal pieces, so one piece is $\frac16$.
$$\frac12\div3=\frac16$$

answer.worked:

$$\frac12\div5=\frac1{10}$$
